about.title: Riverbank Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Riverbank's traffic pattern is shaped by a handful of busy corridors — Patterson Road, Oakdale Road, Claribel Road, and Rt 108 — where public records show the bulk of local injury collisions occur, often clustering around Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. In a recent year, Stanislaus County recorded 103 injury collisions and 155 injured people connected to Riverbank-area crashes, along with one traffic death. Numbers like these simply reflect how much people move through this small city, not a verdict on any particular street. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: photos, witness names, and vehicle damage can fade or disappear quickly. We handle personal injury claims for Riverbank residents. Our team can review the details of your crash, explain your options, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government vehicle or roadway was involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover a reduced amount. This matters on multi-vehicle corridors like Oakdale Road and Claribel Road where fault can get disputed.

items.title: No Cap Means No Reason to Rush a Statement
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so there's little upside in giving the other driver's insurer a recorded statement early. We can speak for you and make sure evidence is preserved before it disappears.

items.question: What should I do right after a crash on Patterson Road or Rt 108?
items.answer: Get medical attention first, even if the injury seems minor, since some symptoms take days to appear. Take photos of the vehicles, the road, and any visible injuries, and get contact information from witnesses if possible. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've talked to an attorney.

items.question: Do I have to accept the insurance company's first offer?
items.answer: No, and early offers are often lower than what a claim may actually be worth once medical costs and lost time are fully accounted for. Because California doesn't cap pain-and-suffering damages, it's worth having an attorney review any offer before you sign anything. There's no obligation to accept the first number presented.

items.question: What if the crash happened at a Riverbank intersection controlled by the city or Caltrans?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads or signals come with a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes as short as six months instead of the usual two years. This is common on higher-volume roads like Oakdale Road or Claribel Road. Because of that shortened window, it's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible after the crash.
